tutorial.title: Tutorials
tutorial.start.title: Getting started
tutorial.start.body:
You News has three columns: headings on the left, the headline list in the middle, and the story on the right.

  1. Pick a heading on the left to switch topics.
  2. Use the hours menu above the list to show only recent stories.
  3. Press Refresh (F5) to pull the latest feeds.
  4. Open Tutorials anytime from the left, Settings, or F1.
tutorial.headings.title: Headings and time window
tutorial.headings.body:
The left tree is your news map. Parent counts are the sum of their children.

  1. Click a main heading (for example Economy) to see all of its stories.
  2. Open a subheading to narrow the list.
  3. Archive at the bottom shows saved stories only.
  4. Ctrl+E expands the tree; Ctrl+Shift+E collapses it.
tutorial.sources.title: Add and remove sources
tutorial.sources.body:
Feeds live on this computer. Built-in sources can be turned off but not deleted.

  1. Open Settings → Sources.
  2. Enter a name and an http(s) RSS URL, pick a module, then Add.
  3. Use Test to confirm headlines arrive before you rely on the feed.
  4. Uncheck Active to pause a source. Only sources you added can be removed.
  5. You can also paste a news site URL in the assistant chat to add it.
tutorial.filters.title: Filters
tutorial.filters.body:
Filters hide or keep headlines by keyword.

  1. Open Settings → Filters.
  2. Type a keyword (company, country, or topic).
  3. Choose Blacklist to hide matching stories.
  4. Choose Whitelist to show only matching stories. If any whitelist exists, everything else is hidden.
  5. Select a row and Remove to delete it.
tutorial.social.title: Social media follows
tutorial.social.body:
Follow public RSS accounts under the Social media heading.

  1. Open Settings → Social media, or use Follow on an empty Social media list.
  2. Paste a YouTube, Substack, or Bluesky link (or a handle).
  3. Press Test to see the latest posts, then Follow.
  4. Select a row and Unfollow to remove it. Limit is 20 accounts.
tutorial.tickers.title: Watchlist and tape
tutorial.tickers.body:
The top tape shows live Yahoo Finance quotes.

  1. Click Watchlist on the tape, or Settings → Tickers.
  2. Search by name (Toyota, petrol, Türkiye). Presets appear first; Yahoo then lists matching symbols worldwide.
  3. Add or remove symbols. Click a quote to pin related headlines.
tutorial.save.title: Save, emoji, archive
tutorial.save.body:
Stories older than 24 hours are removed unless you save them.

  1. Open a story on the right.
  2. Press Save so it stays in Archive.
  3. Pick an emoji to mark it. Saved items change color in the list.
  4. Open Archive at the bottom of the left tree to find them.
tutorial.ai.title: AI summary and translate
tutorial.ai.body:
Summaries and translations use your own API key or local Ollama.

  1. Add a key in Settings (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, or Ollama).
  2. Open a story and press Summarize. The right-hand title is translated to the app language automatically when a key is set.
  3. The middle list always keeps the original headline.
  4. Use Translate for the full article body. Briefing buttons above the list summarize a time window or your selection.
tutorial.listen.title: Listen to a summary
tutorial.listen.body:
Windows voices read the right-hand summary. This does not slow the news list.

  1. Open a story (prefer one with an AI summary).
  2. Choose Female or Male.
  3. Press Listen. Turkish, English, and Spanish use installed voices when available.
  4. Press Stop to end playback.
tutorial.chat.title: News assistant
tutorial.chat.body:
The assistant only talks about news in this app.

  1. Open the news assistant from the left.
  2. Ask about markets, a company, or a country.
  3. Paste a news site or RSS URL to add it as a source.
  4. Matching headlines appear as clickable stories.
app.about_license: You News is a Windows desktop news reader. Headlines and settings stay on this PC. AI uses your own API key or local Ollama — we do not sell model access.
app.disclaimer:
You News is an independent reader — not a Yahoo, Microsoft, or newsroom product. The market tape shows Yahoo Finance figures through yfinance. Numbers can lag; they’re a glance, not investment advice.

Headlines and article text stay with their publishers. You add a source; You News fetches it for you to read. We don’t sell that writing.

Website purchases use Paddle.com as Merchant of Record (payment, support, refunds). Sales are planned through younews.media for now.
